title: Shortcut Conflict shown when there's no documented conflict.

judgment.rationale: The detector has a confirmed generic system-conflict fallback and the reported shortcut is functional on Windows 11, but the exact OS heuristic needs tracing.
evidence: Reporter reproduced on current stable Windows 11.
Win+Shift+C activates Color Picker without functional conflict.
Detector source falls back to HasConflictWithSystemHotkey and can synthesize a System entry.
Related #50402 indicates broader unknown-origin conflict work.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve an OS-aware detector design after tracing the system-hotkey heuristic.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete fix attempt was found for #50239; related #50402 is separate live work.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys reports a system shortcut conflict for Color Picker Win+Shift+C on Windows 11 even though the linked shortcut list has no matching active shortcut and activation works. The detector's fallback path is the key triage lead.
known_information: Issue is open and labeled Product-General.
Reporter confirmed behavior on 0.101.2362 and Windows 11 build 26200.
hotkey_conflict_detector.cpp checks maps then calls HasConflictWithSystemHotkey; GetAllConflicts can synthesize a System entry.
inferences: The warning may be a stale Windows-version heuristic or fallback classification rather than a functional conflict.
This may be broader than Color Picker.
issue_context.analysis: The report is reproducible and detector source has an explicit generic fallback. A focused design should identify the system-hotkey table/heuristic and gate deprecated shortcuts by OS/version.
initial_investigation: Read full discussion and current-version confirmation.

information_gaps.information: The detector's system-hotkey result for Win+Shift+C on Windows 11 and Windows 10
information_gaps.why_needed: Separates stale OS mapping from key normalization or fallback behavior
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Capture a focused detector/debug trace with OS build for Win+Shift+C on both versions

proposed_fixes.title: Make system shortcut conflict detection OS-aware and evidence-based
proposed_fixes.root_cause: After registered maps miss, the detector can classify a shortcut as System through a heuristic/fallback that may treat deprecated Win+Shift+C as active on Windows 11.
plan: Locate and document the system-hotkey table/heuristic.
Represent availability by Windows version or remove inactive mappings.
Do not synthesize a System conflict without positive evidence.
Add detector tests for Win+Shift+C and genuine system conflicts.
verification: Set Color Picker to Win+Shift+C on Windows 11 and verify no indicator.
Verify known active conflicts still report.

confidence.rationale: The fallback is confirmed, but the exact system-hotkey heuristic and OS matrix need tracing.

design.root_cause: The detector can synthesize a System conflict after registered maps miss, and a historical shortcut rule may be applied on Windows 11 without current evidence.
evidence: hotkey_conflict_detector.cpp checks sys/in-app maps before HasConflictWithSystemHotkey.
GetAllConflicts creates a System fallback when maps miss.
Win+Shift+C works for Color Picker and is absent from the linked current list.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Unknown unmapped shortcuts can become System conflicts through heuristic/fallback.
implementation_steps.change: Require positive evidence and apply OS-version-aware mappings; return no conflict for inactive deprecated mappings.
implementation_steps.code_block: if (systemHotkeyTable.Contains(osBuild, hotkey)) return SystemConflict; return NoConflict;

verify: Manually set Color Picker to Win+Shift+C on Windows 11.
risks: Windows shortcut knowledge can become stale.
Removing fallback warnings may hide unknown conflicts.
alternatives: Change only help link; rejected because indicator remains false-positive.

comment.body: The detector checks registered maps and then falls back to HasConflictWithSystemHotkey, while the issue confirms Win+Shift+C activates Color Picker on Windows 11. Please capture the detector's result for Win+Shift+C on Windows 11 and Windows 10, including OS build. This distinguishes a stale mapping from an overly broad fallback without hiding genuine conflicts.
